{{Short description|Series of DVDs}}
'''''Looney Tunes Super Stars''''' is a series of nine [[Looney Tunes]] DVDs consisting of two ''Bugs Bunny'' DVDs and other characters who got their own collections. It started on August 10, 2010, and ran until April 23, 2013. The series consists of:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Looney-Tunes-Super-Stars/13168 |title=Date, Titles for New DVDs featuring Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100102084240/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Looney-Tunes-Super-Stars/13168 |archivedate=2010-01-02 |website=tvshowsondvd.com |date=December 30, 2009}}</ref>

Although ''Super Stars'' is the semi-successor{{clarify|date=March 2025}} to the ''[[Looney Tunes Golden Collection]]'' series, the true successor{{clarify|date=March 2025}} to the ''Golden Collection'' is the ''Looney Tunes Platinum Collection''{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}. However, unlike the ''Platinum Collection'', there are no special features in the ''Super Stars'' series. While other volumes were planned, no further releases were made after 2013.<ref>Jerry Beck, on Stu Show 11.</ref> The ''Pepe Le Pew: Zee Best of Zee Best'' and the ''Sylvester & Hippety Hopper: Marsupial Mayhem'' DVDs are now the only home media releases from [[Warner Bros. Discovery Home Entertainment]] to have a major Looney Tunes character's (and two minor Looney Tunes characters') entire filmography featured.

'''''Looney Tunes Super Stars' Pepé Le Pew: Zee Best of Zee Best''''' was released on December 27, 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Looney-Tunes-Super-Stars/15875 |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2011-09-01 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307045052/http://tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Looney-Tunes-Super-Stars/15875 |archivedate=2012-03-07 |website=tvshowsondvd.com |date=September 1, 2011}}</ref> The pre-53 shorts are presented in full screen while the post-53 shorts have both widescreen and full screen options (except for 1956's "Heaven Scent" which is only available in full screen).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goldenagecartoons.com/reviews/2011/pepe/ |title=Golden Age Cartoons &#124; Reviews &#124; Looney Tunes Super Stars: Pepe le Pew |accessdate=2011-12-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120509125149/http://www.goldenagecartoons.com/reviews/2011/pepe/ |archivedate=2012-05-09 }}</ref> This was also the last Looney Tunes Super Stars series to feature a matted 1:85 widescreen format option for the post-1953 shorts and one of the few Warner Bros. home media release to feature the entire filmography of a major Looney Tunes character.

All cartoons on this disc feature [[Pepé Le Pew]].

=== Notes ===
* According to Jerry Beck, the reason the two Bunny and Claude cartoons were included on the DVD was for filler.
* While the set claims that all the cartoons on the set are "remastered for the first time into pristine, first-run condition," ''Wagon Heels'' and ''Boobs in the Woods'' were previously released restored on the ''[[Looney Tunes Golden Collection: Volume 5]]'' DVD and the ''[[Looney Tunes Golden Collection: Volume 1]]'' DVD, respectively. In addition, ''One Meat Brawl'' uses an unrestored USA 1995 dubbed version transfer and ''Ant Pasted'' uses the 1998 dubbed version transfer, hence the cue marks at the iris out and the closing of the rings. A restored version of ''One Meat Brawl'' was released on ''[[Looney Tunes Collector's Choice#Volume 2|Looney Tunes Collector's Choice: Volume 2]]'' Blu-ray.
* On the back of the DVD, photos of ''Tick Tock Tuckered'', ''[[Daffy Doodles]]'', and ''Nothing but the Tooth'' are shown—however, these cartoon aren't actually included on the DVD. ''Tick Tock Tuckered'' was released on ''Looney Tunes Super Stars' Daffy Duck: Frustrated Fowl''; ''Daffy Doodles'' appears as an extra on the DVD of the Warner Bros. movie ''[[My Reputation]]'', using the 1995 USA dubbed version transfer, and was later released in a restored form on the ''[[Looney Tunes Collector's Choice#Volume 1|Looney Tunes Collector's Choice: Volume 1]]'' Blu-ray; ''Nothing but the Tooth'' will be released on the ''[[Looney Tunes Collector's Vault#Volume 3|Looney Tunes Collector's Vault: Volume 3]]'' Blu-ray.
* The PAL version of the DVD includes ''One Meat Brawl'' with the red borders at the opening titles as it was sourced from the 1995 PAL Dubbed Version print.
* ''Ant Pasted'' 1953 English audiotrack on PAL DVD release is played with low-pitched audio.

'''''Looney Tunes Super Stars' Sylvester & Hippety Hopper: Marsupial Mayhem''''' is a DVD featuring 18 newly remastered cartoons. It is the final release in the ''Super Star'' series, due to poor sales of ''[[Looney Tunes Platinum Collection: Volume 2]]'' and the depletion of the remastering budget for new-to-DVD ''Looney Tunes'' shorts.<ref name="TV Shows on DVD">{{cite web | title = The Bugs Bunny/Looney Tunes Comedy Hour DVD news: Announcement for Looney Tunes Super Stars' Sylvester & Hippety Hopper: Marsupial Mayhem | date = January 16, 2013 | url = http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Looney-Tunes-Super-Stars/17964 | accessdate = April 15, 2013 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20130421072300/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Looney-Tunes-Super-Stars/17964 | archivedate = April 21, 2013 }}</ref> This release features all 18 of Sylvester's pairings with Hippety Hopper and/or his son, Sylvester Jr. The DVD was released on April 23, 2013.<ref name="TV Shows on DVD" />

All cartoons in this collection star [[Sylvester the Cat|Sylvester]], and co-star either [[Hippety Hopper]] and/or [[Sylvester Jr.]] All are directed by [[Robert McKimson]], except for ''[[Goldimouse and the Three Cats]]'', which was directed by [[Friz Freleng]].

== Reception ==
The first two ''Looney Tunes Super Stars'' sets (''Bugs Bunny: Hare Extraordinaire'' and ''Daffy Duck: Frustrated Fowl'') had released the majority the cartoons from the post-1953 era in a 1:85 widescreen format. Warner Bros. has stated the reason for this was because that is how the post-1953 cartoons were shown in theaters, though the cartoons were filmed in Academy ratio, not widescreen at that time. On December 1, 2010, animation expert [[Jerry Beck]] explained on the Shokus Internet Radio call-in talk program, ''Stu's Show'' that Warner aimed this series, not at collectors, but at the mass market who expect it to fit on their widescreen TVs. He speculated that at some point down the road there would probably be a double-dip release of those shorts in a collector's DVD version with the video in full-frame format. However, the [[Foghorn Leghorn]] DVD includes both the widescreen and the Academy ratio of the cartoons on the same disc and further releases provide only fullscreen viewing.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://forums.goldenagecartoons.com/showthread.php?p=181212#post181212 |title= Foghorn Leghorn DVD contains option for standard or widescreen - GAC Forums|website=forums.goldenagecartoons.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101220010830/http://forums.goldenagecartoons.com/showthread.php?p=181212 |archive-date=2010-12-20}}</ref>

On the ''Tweety and Sylvester: Feline Fwenzy'' and ''Bugs Bunny: Wascally Wabbit'' DVDs, all of the cartoons have been released previously on the ''Golden Collection'' series, much to the disappointment of fans.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Stu%27s-Show-Jerry-Beck/14771 |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2012-11-16 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004232950/http://tvshowsondvd.com/news/Bugs-Bunny-Looney-Tunes-Comedy-Hour-Stu%27s-Show-Jerry-Beck/14771 |archivedate=2012-10-04 }}</ref>

With the ''Road Runner and Wile E. Coyote: Supergenius Hijinks'' DVD, some collectors were disappointed that the set focused on the less well-received [[DePatie–Freleng Enterprises|DFE]]-era Coyote/Road Runner cartoons (particularly the [[Rudy Larriva]]-directed ones) and lacked [[Chuck Jones]]' Coyote/Road Runner cartoons from the pre-1964 "classic" era.
